clue.text: Ordinary horse — spotted one with teeth

parts.note: a hack is a horse for ordinary riding, or for hire
saw means spotted, caught sight of

explanation.surface: A description of a plain horse with a spotted coat and a set of teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting tool for metal has a toothed blade, so it is cryptically something with teeth.

clue.text: Taunt flipping partner leading empty life

indicators.note: leading puts the oath's partner in front

parts.note: heck partners flipping in the mild oath 'flipping heck'

indicators.note: empty means the inside of the word is removed, leaving its outside letters

parts.note: first and last letters of life

explanation.surface: Mocking a partner who has flipped and leads a hollow life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping heck' is a mild British exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: To shout jeering interruptions at a speaker is to barrack or jeer them.

clue.text: Best frozen treat, no longer cold in the middle

indicators.note: no longer says the letter for cold is dropped
in the middle says the dropped letter is the central one

parts.note: a choc ice is a chocolate-coated ice-cream bar
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: The finest ice-cream treat, no longer chilled inside.
explanation.walkthrough: A choc ice is a British ice-cream bar coated in chocolate; remove its middle C.
explanation.definitionFit: The pick of the bunch, the selection one prefers, is the finest, as an adjective.

clue.text: Mix up in heart of Brussels, nothing concerning but a pain in the backside

indicators.note: in puts the muddle word between the two letters
heart of means the central letters of the word

parts.note: middle two letters of Brussels
to addle is to muddle, mix up
O looks like zero, nothing
re means concerning, about

explanation.surface: A confusion at the heart of the EU in Brussels, trivial but annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider who has been long in the saddle is chafed, with an ache in the buttocks.

clue.text: Lavish women like terribly expensive originals

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: originals means the first letters of the words

parts.note: first letter of terribly
first letter of expensive

explanation.surface: Extravagant women who favour very costly originals.
explanation.definitionFit: To lavish money on something can mean to squander it, spending it freely and uselessly.

clue.text: Aussie's encouragement for Hampshire town

definitions.meaning: first meaning: '...!', a cheer an Australian might give a mate
second meaning: a naval town on the Hampshire coast, opposite Portsmouth

explanation.walkthrough: Split as GO SPORT, the town's name is an Australian cry of support; Hampshire is a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The place is a real town in Hampshire, home to naval establishments across the harbour from Portsmouth.

clue.text: American soldier arrests a foul-mouthed Italian general

indicators.note: arrests means the soldier holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a GI is a US soldier
ribald means coarse or vulgar in speech

explanation.surface: A US soldier detaining a swearing Italian military commander.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Garibaldi was the soldier who led the campaigns that unified Italy in the 19th century.

clue.text: Power boat deviates from course, capsizing

indicators.note: capsizing turns things upside down, so the word is read the other way, bottom to top

parts.note: a boat that yaws swings off its course

explanation.surface: A powerboat veering off course and overturning.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding sway means holding power and influence over others.

clue.text: Views duck wings

parts.note: a duck is a score of zero in cricket, the letter O
pinions are birds' wings

explanation.surface: Looking at the wings of a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's views are their opinions, beliefs held on a subject.

clue.text: Breaking into spring-loaded lock …

indicators.note: loaded means the lock is filled with the spring's letters

parts.note: a lock of hair is a tress
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: A burglar forcing a spring-loaded lock, continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring-loaded' reads as one engineering term but splits into a spring and a loading.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlawfully going onto property is entering it without permission, an intrusion.

clue.text: Mass murder participant died

parts.note: a group of crows is called a murder, so a crow takes part in one
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A mass killing with one of the people involved having died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Murder' is the collective noun for crows, not a crime here.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of people gathered together is a throng, the noun sense of the answer.

clue.text: On the radio, breakfast item is expected at first to air in several parts

indicators.note: something heard on the radio is only heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: cereal is a breakfast food

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: first letter of expected

explanation.surface: A radio item about breakfast food being expected to be broadcast in instalments.
explanation.walkthrough: CEREAL sounds like SERIAL; add IS and the E from 'expected'.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast a story in instalments is to put it out episode by episode.

clue.text: Slimming wine knocked over by neighbours in confrontation

parts.note: lo-cal, low in calories, describes slimming food

indicators.note: a glass knocked over is upended, so the word for the wine is turned backwards

parts.note: red is a wine

explanation.surface: Diet wine spilt by people next door during a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slimming' suggests weight loss, but here it describes food that is low in calories.
explanation.definitionFit: A local derby is a sporting match between teams from the same area, near neighbours meeting as rivals.

clue.text: Liz Truss reflects after women's organisation's "ineffectual person" label

indicators.note: after places the reversed piece behind the organisation's letters

parts.note: WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the other way round, so the title is read backwards

parts.note: Liz Truss was briefly the UK's PM, Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A former prime minister musing on a label the Women's Institute pinned on her.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute is a British organisation known for a famous slow handclap of a prime minister; PM reversed gives MP.
explanation.definitionFit: A weak, timid person lacking courage or force is commonly called this, a mild insult.

clue.text: … anaemic pet runs free

indicators.note: runs as in a colour running suggests the letters lose their order

explanation.surface: A sickly pet escapes, following on from the break-in clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate someone from slavery or control is to set them at liberty.

clue.text: Adds to "Vitamin and Mineral" magazines?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to supplement is to add to
second meaning: vitamin and mineral pills are dietary ...
third meaning: newspaper colour magazines are called ...

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks dress Vitamin and Mineral up as magazine titles, but each sense stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means extra additions, as verb, as pills taken for health, and as the extra sections of a newspaper.

clue.text: Overheard instruction to perform composer's selected recordings

indicators.note: overheard means the words are taken by how they sound

parts.note: play is an instruction to perform music; Liszt was a Hungarian composer

explanation.surface: Someone overhearing a request to perform a composer's chosen recordings.
explanation.definitionFit: Lists of songs chosen to be played in order are sequences of tracks picked for listening.

clue.text: A large amount of stuff that's fallen off the back of a lorry?

definitions.text: A large amount of stuff that's fallen off the back of a lorry?

parts.words: A large amount of stuff that's fallen off the back of a lorry?
parts.note: a slang word for a great deal, read literally as what a lorry has spilt from its back

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, goods that 'fell off the back of a lorry' are stolen; here the lorry literally sheds its cargo.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a great quantity, read literally as a vehicle's cargo being dropped.

clue.text: No longer in job, so let empty houses

indicators.note: houses says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: No longer employed, so the house is left empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Something outdated is no longer in use, superseded by something newer.

clue.text: Swimming in hot brine, a winter relaxation

indicators.note: swimming suggests things moving about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bathing in hot salty water as a way to unwind in winter.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals spend the cold season dormant, a long sleep through winter that is a kind of rest.

clue.text: Spooner's refreshing drink for exercise class?

indicators.note: Spooner's means the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: chai is spiced tea, a refreshing brew
tea is a drink; said aloud it is the sound written TI here, so swapping opening sounds with CHAI gives the second word

explanation.surface: The Reverend Spooner asking for a drink before a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: Say CHAI TEA with the opening sounds swapped and you get TAI CHI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chinese martial art practised as slow, flowing movements is often taught as a fitness session.

clue.text: Standing stone tops American tours regularly

indicators.note: tops means the stone's letters go above the rest in this down answer

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken

parts.note: odd letters of tours

explanation.surface: A standing stone crowning the regular tours of American visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's standing is their rank or position in society.

clue.text: Yes, certainly not an Arab vessel

indicators.note: not says the word an is left out of the exclamation

parts.note: 'And how!' is an emphatic yes, certainly
taken as written

explanation.surface: An emphatic denial that something is an Arab ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes, certainly' gives AND HOW; 'not an' takes away the A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional sailing boat with a lateen sail, used on the Arabian Sea and Red Sea.

clue.text: 3-D modelling a cryptic representation of rat?

parts.note: read as wordplay, plastic signals an anagram of ART, which makes the clue's word rat

explanation.surface: Building a model of a rat in three dimensions, with a crossword-style depiction.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says outright that the answer is cryptic wordplay for 'rat': 'plastic' is an anagram signal, and its fodder ART rearranges to RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sculpture and modelling in three dimensions are known as the shaping arts, from Greek for moulding.

clue.text: Video call from Blue Peter's first couple

parts.note: the sky is blue, and blue can mean the sky

indicators.note: first couple means the first two letters of the word

parts.note: first two letters of Peter

explanation.surface: A video call from the children's programme Blue Peter's first couple of presenters.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue Peter is a long-running British children's TV programme.
explanation.definitionFit: The trade name is so familiar it stands for an internet video call itself.

clue.text: Instinct to pry into wine quality

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an instinct for it
second meaning: to ... into something is to pry
third meaning: a wine's ... is its aroma

explanation.walkthrough: Three separate senses of one word; 'to' and 'into' link them, and 'nose into' is the phrasal form for prying.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ of smell lends its name to intuition, to snooping, and to the bouquet of wine.

clue.text: Heavily rely on us going off chasing love

indicators.note: chasing means the rearranged letters follow behind the zero

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: going off suggests the words go wrong, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone depending heavily on others whose interest is waning while chasing romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in a burdensome way, weighing heavily on someone, as with an onerous task.

clue.text: Tie coats up

indicators.note: up as in stirred up or mixed up says the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An instruction to fasten coats.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad neck scarf worn instead of a necktie, named after the racecourse.

clue.text: Weightwatchers finish with detailed brief

parts.note: to die is to finish, come to an end

indicators.note: read as de-tailed, the word loses its tail, its last letter

parts.note: terse means brief

explanation.surface: A short, detailed brief ending a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: People on a slimming regime watch their weight, so they are the ones restricting food.

clue.text: Pharmacists cite measures restricting return of medicines

indicators.note: return of says the hidden run is read backwards
restricting means the words hold the letters within them

explanation.surface: Chemists quoting dosage measures that limit how often medicines are given back.
explanation.definitionFit: Drugs that cause vomiting are a class of medical treatment, given to purge poisons.
